Who bills what in Portland

  • Multnomah County property tax office - handles values and tax collection handles assessment.

Due dates

Multnomah payment FAQ: payments due Nov 15 (next business day if weekend/holiday); 3% discount for full payment, 2% for 2/3 with final due May 15; 1/3 payment with Feb 15 and May 15 installments. A Multnomah news-release headline (search result only) states payments due Nov. 16, 2026.. See the official page.

Challenging your assessment

Petition to the Property Values Appeals Board (formerly BOPTA) must be postmarked or delivered by December 31 after the current-year tax statement is available; accepted by mail or in person only.. See the official page.

Portland by the numbers

Which county bills property tax for a Portland house?

For most Portland addresses it is Multnomah County. The city covers about 145 square miles, nearly all in Multnomah County, with small parts in Clackamas and Washington counties.

If your house sits in one of those small slivers, confirm the billing office with that county before you rely on anything here. The Multnomah pages we reviewed cover Multnomah accounts only.

Portland sits where the Willamette and Columbia rivers meet, about 60 miles inland from the Pacific. The Willamette divides the city into east and west sides, and Burnside Street splits north from south. Since South Portland was added in 2020, the city uses six addressing sectors: N, NE, NW, S, SE and SW.

Portland housing and income figures from the Census Bureau

The Census Bureau estimates Portland's population at 635,109 for July 1, 2025. About 52.0% of homes are owner-occupied, and the median value of an owner-occupied home was $581,500 for 2020 to 2024.

What does the Portland economy and climate mean for a house sale?

Portland's economy rests on technology, athletic and outdoor brands, shipping through the Port of Portland and craft industries such as breweries. Leading employers in 2024 included Intel, Oregon Health and Science University, Providence Health and Services, Kaiser Foundation and Nike.

The climate is wet and cool in winter and warm and dry in summer. Portland averages about 157 days a year with measurable precipitation, and only about 4.3 inches of snow. The all-time record high of 116 degrees Fahrenheit came in June 2021 during a regional heat wave.

For a seller, long wet seasons make roofs and drainage the first things a buyer checks. Heat waves like the 2021 one draw attention to older homes too.

How do Portland's transit, neighborhoods and government affect sellers?

Location relative to MAX and major highways often matters as much as the house itself. TriMet runs most regional buses and the MAX light rail, which opened in 1986 and now has five lines. I-5 runs north-south, I-405 loops downtown, I-205 loops the east side to the airport, and I-84 leads toward Boise.

Portland International Airport is about 20 minutes by car or 40 by MAX from downtown. The city-owned Portland Streetcar has two routes, and Tilikum Crossing opened in 2015.

  • Portland has 95 officially recognized neighborhoods, each with a volunteer association, grouped under seven district coalitions.
  • Since January 1, 2025, the city runs on a mayor and 12-member council, elected from four districts.
  • Metro, the only directly elected metropolitan planning body in the country, handles regional land use and transportation.
  • Portland's urban growth boundary was adopted in 1979, which sets the outer line for urban growth.

What are the key Multnomah County property tax dates for Portland owners?

For 2026, payments are due November 16, 2026, and appeals are due by December 31, 2026. Property values are as of January 1, 2026, and the county mailed about 300,000 statements and value notices, which owners should have received by November 1.

DateEvent
January 1, 2026Value date for the 2026 tax roll
November 16, 2026First payment due; 3% discount for full payment, 2% for two-thirds
December 31, 2026Last day for a value appeal, by USPS postmark or delivery
February 16, 2027Second installment due on the three-payment plan
First Monday in February to April 15Appeals hearings
May 17, 2027Third installment due

The county states that Oregon law sets the due date, and the county cannot extend it or waive late interest. Offices were closed November 11, 2026 for Veterans Day.

How do Portland owners pay, and how big is the county tax bill overall?

Owners can pay online, by phone, by mail, at a 24-hour drop box or in person at the Multnomah Building, 501 SE Hawthorne Blvd. Online payments through proptax.multco.us can come straight from a bank account, and convenience fees apply.

  • Phone: 503-988-2225, Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • In person: Suite 175, weekdays, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • Mail: P.O. Box 2716, Portland, OR 97208-2716, postmarked by the due date.
  • Drop box: checks only, no cash.

Across all taxing districts, 2026 taxes in Multnomah County total $2.602 billion, up about 3.5% from $2.515 billion in 2025. If a payment has not processed by December 1, call customer service.

A yellow statement means a party such as a mortgage lender requested the bill. Check with that party before you pay, so the same installment is not paid twice.

How do you read a Portland property tax statement?

The statement shows real market value, which is the assessor's estimate of market value as of January 1, and assessed value, which is the lower of real market value or maximum assessed value. Each taxing district on the bill collects a permanent rate for ongoing services, plus any extra taxes voters approved.

Multnomah sorts those district levies into three groups: education, general government, and bond taxes. Questions about a specific levy go to the district that imposes it, not to the county. Payments all go to the Multnomah County Tax Collector.

A Portland seller can use the statement to estimate what the buyer will inherit. Because assessed value is generally the lower figure, the bill will not match what a house would sell for today.

How does a Portland property value appeal work?

File a petition with the Property Values Appeals Board, postmarked or delivered by December 31, using the U.S. Postal Service postmark rather than a postage meter. The board is a panel of private citizens appointed by the Multnomah County Board of Commissioners, and it is separate from the Assessor's Office.

  • The fee is $30 per account, and each account needs its own petition. Appeals are accepted by mail or in person only, not by email or fax.
  • The appeal must show market value as of January 1 and prove the assessor's value is too high.
  • Evidence can include an arm's-length sale near January 1, a fee appraisal, or comparable sales with differences accounted for.
  • Hearings run from the first Monday in February through April 15 at the Multnomah Building, usually about 15 minutes each.

The board decides on the hearing day, and a written order follows, usually within a week. A refund is mailed later. A disagreement with the board can go to Oregon Tax Court, and the written decision explains how.

What happens if Portland property tax goes unpaid?

Interest accrues at 1.3333% per month on the delinquent balance after the 15th of each month, and real property becomes subject to foreclosure three years after the earliest delinquency. Taxes are a lien on July 1, at the start of a tax year that runs July 1 to June 30.

The county's example: 2021 taxes that became delinquent on May 16, 2022 became subject to foreclosure in May 2025. Owners in foreclosure get mailed notices that explain the steps and payment deadlines.

Any payment goes to the oldest tax owed. To avoid escalated collection, owners can ask for a payment plan through the county's delinquent tax request form, or call Tax Collections at 503-988-3334. Under Oregon's foreclosure statutes, a property that goes through judgment is held by the county for two years before it can be redeemed or lost.

How does selling a Portland house with tax due usually work?

The title or escrow company requests a payoff from the county and pays unpaid tax from the seller's proceeds at closing. Recording the deed in Multnomah County costs $86 for the first page and $5 for each added page, which the closing statement will show.

If you inherited a Portland house or own one with back taxes, ask the county what is owed before you list, and keep in mind the three-year foreclosure clock. We buy Portland houses as-is, so you do not need to repair the roof or clear the yard to ask for an offer. Send us the address and any tax notices you have.

More questions about Portland, OR Property Tax Guide

Who do I pay Portland property tax to?

Most Portland owners pay the Multnomah County Tax Collector, at 501 SE Hawthorne Blvd, Suite 175, or online at proptax.multco.us. Houses in the parts of Portland inside Clackamas or Washington County are billed by those counties.

When is Portland property tax due in 2026?

November 16, 2026 for the first payment. Paying in full by then earns a 3% discount, and paying two-thirds earns 2%. The installment plan adds payments on February 16, 2027 and May 17, 2027.

How do I appeal my Portland property value?

Send a petition with a $30 fee per account to the Property Values Appeals Board, postmarked or delivered by December 31. Hearings run from the first Monday in February through April 15.

What interest rate applies to late property tax in Multnomah County?

Interest runs at 1.3333% per month on the delinquent balance after the 15th of each month. Foreclosure becomes possible three years after the earliest delinquency.

Can I sell my Portland house if I owe property tax?

Yes. Unpaid tax is usually paid from the sale proceeds at closing, and the county or the title company can give you a payoff figure.
